Sampled ranking measures performance against its candidate distribution; it does not establish full-catalog quality. RecSys 2025 research separates exposure bias from evaluation-sampling bias and evaluates sampling through model separability, agreement with full evaluation, robustness, and alignment with true preferences. For RecHarness, preserve the pinned 99-negative evaluator and macro validation HR@10 selection; any permitted candidate-sampling or full-catalog checks should be supplementary diagnostics. [Pereira et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398).

Training-negative choices can produce subgroup trade-offs hidden by averages. A 2024 sequential-recommendation study found random negatives favored head items, while popularity-based negatives balanced popularity-band performance at some overall accuracy cost. Separately, reproduction research found popularity-bias conclusions strongly dependent on evaluation strategy and user grouping. The 2026 negative-sampling survey highlights that hard negatives may actually be unobserved positives. These findings motivate popularity and history-length strata, but do not establish individual false negatives from implicit histories. [Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276); [Daniil et al., 2024](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/33989); [Ma et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1145/3793855).

Practical synthesis: predefine strata using training histories, report subgroup counts and per-user hit changes, and use paired user bootstrap resampling within each category before recomputing the four-category macro difference. These intervals capture user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and seed, not training or candidate-sampling variability. Distributional evaluation research supports examining uncertainty and heterogeneous benefits. Treat a diagnostic as actionable only when a controlled intervention targeting its hypothesized failure improves validation ranking in the predicted subgroup and supports the macro objective. Keep one HSTU model per category and seed 42; bootstrap predictions without retraining or averaging models. [Ekstrand et al., 2024](https://doi.org/10.1145/3613455).
